text:
jin: Heads-up — during veridian-lite-v2 int8 onboarding I saw a sharp spike in sampling entropy for zh/ko outputs compared to en. Quality drop in our locale BLEU and some tokenization oddities. Anyone seen sampling entropy behave like this with quantized kernels? :thinking:
kevin: Can you paste a minimal repro + numbers?
jin: Quick summary and sample run below. This was on dedicated-staging, quant=int8, sampler=top-p 0.92, temp=0.8.
```
# stats by locale (n=128 samples each)
locale  mean_entropy  var_entropy  kl_vs_en
en      3.1           0.45         0.00
zh      5.7           1.8          1.9
ko      5.4           1.5          1.7
ar      4.0           0.6          0.9
# sample where we see strange subtoken breaks (zh)
src: "请提供最新的产品文档。"
sample1: "请 提供 最新 的 产 品 文 档 。"
sample2: "请提供最新的 产品 文档。"
```
kevin: wow entropy jump is huge. Could be tokenization mismatch or sampling amplifying a subtle logits noise from quant kernel. Did you compare float vs int8 logits distribution?
sam: run argmax/deterministic sampling vs stochastic to narrow it down. If argmax is fine but sampling explodes, it's likely variance in tail logits.
jin: ran quick compare: argmax top-1 seqs are stable and BLEU ~ baseline. Sampling (temp 0.8) gives the degraded BLEU and the token split noise. I also captured logits dump for a single prefix — attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/xxxx (shows long tail with tiny prob mass but many near-equal tokens for CJK subtokens).
anika: two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer aliasing - some byte-level preprocessing path used in int8 build? 2) quantization jitter for embedding/kernel which matters more for CJK subtoken scores because CJK vocab has many near-similar logits. Can you run a controlled eval with `--force-tokenizer utf8-normalize`?
jin: good call. I did `--force-tokenizer utf8-normalize` and entropy dropped ~0.8 for zh but still above en. So tokenizer helped but didn't fully explain.
lili: also check KV-cache path differences in the int8 runtime — we had a recent patch that shortcuts certain fused kernels. That could change attention score precision incrementally.
jin: noted. I added @kevin to run a quick kernel variation matrix (float-kernel with int8-weights vs full-float). Command I used for sampling sweep: 
```
./tools/eval_sampling.py \
  --model veridian-lite-v2 \
  --quant int8 \
  --locales zh,ko,en,ar \
  --sampler top-p=0.92,temp=0.8 \
  --n-samples 128 \
  --out stats.json
```
kevin: I'll kick off a 4x matrix: float-runtime/int8-weights, int8-runtime/int8-weights, float-runtime/float-weights, int8-runtime/float-weights. Should tell us if runtime kernel math is the main offender. ETA ~ 2hrs on staging cluster.
eval-bot: CI sampling-eval veridian-lite-v2 int8 started (run id: ci-6890). Link: https://ci.internal/runs/ci-6890 :spinner:
sam: also try lowering temp to 0.6 and top-k 50 to see sensitivity; if small changes to sampling hyperparams drastically improve BLEU then it's symptomatic of tail instability not tokenizer.
jin: did temp sweep quick: temp=0.6 -> entropy down ~1.2 but BLEU still lower than baseline by ~1.1 points on zh. So hyperparams mitigate but don't restore.
anika: can you bisect on the runtime patch range? I suspect the fused attention precision fix from last month. If we bisect and see a step change in entropy/BLEU we know it's kernel-related.
kevin: agree. I have a candidate range (commit abc123..def456). I'll run a bisect job across the range with the sampling config and reduced n=64 to speed up.
lili: reminder: include locale-specific eval prompts — CJK punctuation adjacency, furigana-like constructs, and mixed-ltr/rtl examples for hybrid test. Those seem to trigger the subtoken splits.
jin: adding a small prompt set: 20 prompts zh news, 20 ko chatty, 10 zh+en mixed, 10 ar+en mixed RTL. I'll drop into /datasets/locale-spotcheck/entropy-set.json
kevin: plan: run kernel matrix + bisect, collect logits diffs and kl scores per locale, tag suspect commit, then produce a small PR reverting kernel change for further test if needed.
anika: if it's kernel precision, we should consider a short-term mitigation: default to temp=0.6 for zh/ko in onboarding docs and flag as known issue in release notes until we fix.
sam: agree. Also add a unit test that compares sampling entropy distribution vs baseline floats for new model onboarding. Prevent regression on future quant builds.
jin: thanks everyone. I'll upload the example sequences and tokenization diffs to the ticket (ML-1129) and assign next actions: @kevin run bisect, @anika curate prompt set, @lili verify kernel flags. Update in ~3h. :thumbsup:
